arguments.document:
The Last Light

Every evening, Mara climbed the lighthouse stairs with a lantern in one hand and a thermos in the other. For forty years, she had watched the waves swallow the sunset and sent a beam back into the dark.

One stormy night, the light went out. Mara hurried to the lamp room, but the old machinery would not turn. Below, a fishing boat pitched helplessly among the rocks.

She grabbed her lantern and ran to the balcony. The flame was small, but she swung it in wide, steady arcs. Through the rain, the boat’s captain spotted her signal and steered clear.

At dawn, the crew came ashore with a new lamp. Mara smiled as they installed it. The lighthouse shone again—but everyone knew whose courage had kept them safe.
